The memo

Overall verdict is outside_evidence: the new traffic signal part is outside_evidence and not scored on this record, so the decision rests on a site study and engineer assessment. The corner shows injury harm with a strong angle pattern, with SDOT as road owner for follow-up.

Dexter Avenue North & John Street had 8 injury crashes in police records since 2021-10-31: 0 people killed. [D4]
88% of crashes here were recorded as entering at angle crashes, against 16% at the city's worst crash locations. [D2]
No crash-modification evidence is applied to the proposed new traffic signal here; it needs its own study and engineer assessment, so the effect is not shown in this record. [D7]
At U.S. DOT values that harm costs about $548,000 a year; proposal cost was not stated, so no benefit-cost ratio is calculated here. [D4]
An eligible alternative, Pavement Friction Management, would avoid about 0.2 crashes a year, worth $74,000 a year, only if a site check confirms low friction now. [D4]
The Seattle Department of Transportation (SDOT) is responsible for Dexter Avenue North, John Street. [D5]
The case against this verdict (4)

Muse Spark Open argued against the verdict. Code kept an objection only if its fact is in the record.

O1 We should be cautious about dismissing the proposal as unsupported. Within 100m since Oct 2021 the record shows a severe, highly over-represented pattern of angle crashes (15 of 17), with meaningful injury harm, suggesting the intersection has a serious gap that a signal could address even without CMF coverage. [D2: over_represented.0.crashes = 15]
Answer: Agreed the angle pattern is severe and over-represented here, which is why a site study and engineer assessment are needed rather than a record-based approval; the signal remains not covered by the evidence used here. [D2]
O2 The site's crash burden is not trivial — 8 injury crashes and 10 persons injured in ~5 years — indicating real safety need that argues for considering intervention on substantive grounds rather than evidentiary classification alone. [D4: crashes.injury_crashes = 8]
Answer: Agreed 8 injury crashes with 0 killed show real harm, which supports asking SDOT to study the site; it does not supply CMF evidence for the signal itself. [D4]
O3 The 'outside evidence' label reflects the federal proven list and CMF availability, not effectiveness at this Stop-controlled location. Angle/entering-at-angle crashes dominate here, which is consistent with control-type conflicts a new signal is intended to manage. [D4: control = Stop-controlled]
Answer: Agreed outside_evidence means no fitting crash-modification record at this Stop-controlled site, not a finding of ineffectiveness; the decision rests on a site study and engineer assessment. [D4]
O4 Even if the signal cannot be scored here, alternative proven treatments targeting the same crash pool show substantial break-even value, implying the underlying crash type is addressable and warrants engineering assessment rather than deference to no coverage. [D4: options.1.break_even_cost_usd = 1808000]
Answer: Agreed the crash pool may be addressable and warrants engineering assessment; the Pavement Friction option illustrates an eligible effect, but it does not score the proposed signal. [D4]
